name: Kontra (Finnish Jass Variant)
description: Kontra is a Finnish Jass game related to the broader family of trick-taking games with trump suits and point-based scoring. Played with partnerships, it features the characteristic elements of Jass games including special trump card rankings and the opportunity for opponents to double ('kontra') the stakes.

history.origins: Kontra belongs to the Jass family of games that originated in Switzerland and spread across Europe. The Finnish variant developed with local adaptations to bidding, scoring, and gameplay. The name 'Kontra' refers to the doubling mechanic common in Jass games.
timeline: 18th Century: Jass games originate in Switzerland
19th Century: Jass spreads to neighboring regions including Finland
20th Century: Finnish Kontra variant develops with local rules
Present: Played in Finland as part of the Jass tradition
history.cultural: Jass games are popular across Northern and Central Europe. In Finland, Kontra represents the local expression of this tradition, played in social and family settings.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Swiss Jass through German and Austrian intermediaries, adapting to Finnish card game preferences. The kontra (doubling) mechanism became a defining feature, allowing opponents to challenge the declaring side.

setup.players: Four players in fixed partnerships (2 vs 2). Partners sit opposite each other.
setup.deck: 32-card French-suited pack (7 through Ace). May also use German-suited cards.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 8 cards, typically dealt in packets (e.g., 3-2-3 or 4-4).

rules.objective: Win tricks containing high-value cards. Partnership needs majority of points (typically 61+ of 120) to win the hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Dealing**: Cards dealt to all players.
2. **Bidding**: Players bid to determine trump suit or play special contracts.
3. **Kontra**: Opponents may say 'Kontra' to double the stakes if they believe declarers will fail.
4. **Trick Play**: Player to dealer's left leads. Must follow suit if possible. If void, may trump or discard.
5. **Winning Tricks**: Highest trump wins, or highest card of led suit. Winner leads to next trick.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; if void, may trump or discard.
Trump Jack (Puur) is the highest card; trump 9 (Nell) is second highest in the game.
Partnership with majority of card points (61+ of 120) wins the hand.
Opponents may say Kontra to double the stakes if they believe the declaring side will fail.
Player to dealer's left leads to the first trick; trick winner leads to the next.

strategy.basic: The trump Jack (20 points) and trump 9 (14 points) are the most powerful cards. Try to win tricks containing these. Count your high cards and plan accordingly.
strategy.intermediate: Trump management is crucial. With many trumps, lead them early to draw out opponents' trumps. Save trumps for winning valuable tricks. Watch which cards have been played.
strategy.advanced: The Kontra decision is strategic. Call Kontra when you believe opponents have overbid or when you have strong defensive cards. Signal to your partner through lead choices. In trump selection, choose suits where you have length and strength.
tips: The trump Jack and 9 are extremely valuable - protect them and use them wisely.
Communication with your partner through card play is essential.
Consider carefully before calling Kontra - it doubles both rewards and penalties.
Track which high cards have been played to calculate remaining winning cards.
